condition.name: tickets-concentrated
condition.what_is_true: 62% of support tickets last quarter came from three workflows: invoice export, SSO setup and bulk import.

option.name: fix-top-workflows
option.we_will: We will fix the three workflows that generate most tickets so that fewer tickets are filed.
option.how: Two engineers for one quarter on invoice export, SSO setup and bulk import.

verdict.case_for: The option targets exactly the three workflows the condition names as the source of 62% of tickets, so the condition is the reason the option exists.
verdict.case_against: The condition says where tickets come from, not that the causes can be fixed in a quarter; some of that volume may be setup questions no fix removes.
verdict.what_changes: If the fixes land, the concentration itself goes away.
verdict.if_it_were_false: If tickets were spread evenly across the product, fixing three workflows would have no case.
verdict.basis: A breakdown of those tickets by cause would move this.

condition.name: tickets-concentrated

option.name: add-support-agents
option.we_will: We will add four support agents so that tickets are answered faster.
option.how: Four hires into the existing support team, trained on enterprise accounts first.

verdict.case_for: Where tickets come from has no bearing on whether more agents answer them faster.
verdict.case_against: Concentration could let new agents specialize, which is a weak positive.
verdict.basis: Whether agents are organized by workflow.

condition.name: tickets-concentrated
condition.what_is_true: 62% of support tickets last quarter came from three workflows: invoice export, SSO setup and bulk import.

option.name: in-app-help
option.we_will: We will put contextual help inside the three workflows so that customers solve problems without filing a ticket.
option.how: Inline guidance and error explanations at the points where tickets are filed today.

verdict.case_for: Help placed inside the three named workflows reaches the point where most tickets start.
verdict.case_against: It assumes customers in those workflows would read help, which this condition says nothing about.
verdict.what_changes: Fewer tickets from those workflows, if the help is used.
verdict.if_it_were_false: With tickets spread evenly there is no small set of screens to put help on.
verdict.basis: Evidence on whether in-context help gets read.

condition.name: enterprise-renewals
condition.what_is_true: Eleven enterprise accounts renew in Q2, and seven of them have open escalations older than 30 days.

option.name: fix-top-workflows
option.we_will: We will fix the three workflows that generate most tickets so that fewer tickets are filed.
option.how: Two engineers for one quarter on invoice export, SSO setup and bulk import.

verdict.case_for: Fewer new tickets would free some agent time for the escalations, a weak and indirect effect.
verdict.case_against: The seven escalations are already open and older than 30 days; fixing workflows this quarter does nothing to close them before the renewals.
verdict.what_changes: A little agent time, late in the quarter.
verdict.if_it_were_false: The option keeps almost all of its case.
verdict.basis: Whether the open escalations sit in the three workflows.

condition.name: enterprise-renewals

option.name: add-support-agents
option.we_will: We will add four support agents so that tickets are answered faster.
option.how: Four hires into the existing support team, trained on enterprise accounts first.

verdict.case_for: Open escalations on renewing accounts are a capacity problem the option addresses directly: more agents, trained on enterprise accounts first.
verdict.case_against: New hires take time to become useful on enterprise escalations, and Q2 may be over before they are.
verdict.what_changes: Escalations get worked sooner once the hires are productive.
verdict.if_it_were_false: Without the renewals the option still answers tickets faster but loses its urgency.
verdict.basis: How long a new agent takes to handle an enterprise escalation alone.

condition.name: release-spikes
condition.what_is_true: Ticket volume rises about 40% in the six weeks after each quarterly release.

option.name: fix-top-workflows
option.we_will: We will fix the three workflows that generate most tickets so that fewer tickets are filed.
option.how: Two engineers for one quarter on invoice export, SSO setup and bulk import.

verdict.case_for: If releases are what break or change these workflows, fixing them reduces the spike at its source.
verdict.case_against: The condition does not say the post-release spike comes from these three workflows.
verdict.what_changes: A smaller spike after each release, if the spike starts there.
verdict.if_it_were_false: The option keeps most of its case without the spikes.
verdict.basis: Ticket mix during the six weeks after a release.

condition.name: release-spikes
condition.what_is_true: Ticket volume rises about 40% in the six weeks after each quarterly release.

option.name: add-support-agents
option.we_will: We will add four support agents so that tickets are answered faster.
option.how: Four hires into the existing support team, trained on enterprise accounts first.

verdict.case_for: Fixed headcount is a poor fit for volume that rises 40% for six weeks a quarter: staffed for the peak it idles, staffed for the average it falls behind.
verdict.case_against: Four more agents still shorten the queue during a spike compared with today.
verdict.if_it_were_false: With flat volume the option would fit better.
verdict.basis: Whether temporary cover is available during spikes.
